result: Of 177 of 341 CFS patients who answered a follow-up questionnaire after about 9 years of illness, 21 (12%) self-reported recovery; better baseline physical and social function and lower anxiety and obsessive-compulsiveness predicted recovery, but with large overlap between groups.
reason: Independent cohort, self-reported recovery rate low, consistent with the finding; also matches the better-outcome-with-milder-baseline detail. Response rate only 52%.

result: In 20 CDC-criteria CFS patients without psychiatric comorbidity vs 20 matched controls, the 1 ug Synacthen test showed no differences in baseline cortisol, peak cortisol, incremental rise or AUC.
reason: Tests the same measure (cortisol response to ACTH stimulation) and finds no blunting; small sample.

result: Telephone screening of 28,673 Chicago adults followed by medical evaluation gave a CFS point prevalence of 0.42% (95% CI 0.29-0.56%), highest in women, minority groups and people with lower education and occupational status.
reason: Random community sample with clinical evaluation; prevalence within the 0.2-1% range and higher in women; not among the cited studies.

result: Of 23 severely ill CFS patients (ill under 4.5 years) followed about 4 years, 13 stayed severely ill, 9 improved but still met 1994 criteria and 1 (4%) recovered; duration, onset mode, psychiatric status and depressed mood did not predict outcome.
reason: Same outcome (recovery rate), very low recovery, but specifically in a severe subgroup, so it extends by severity; very small n.

result: Of 23 severely ill CFS patients followed about 4 years, 13 stayed severe, 9 improved but still met criteria and 1 recovered.
reason: Does not measure the proportion housebound/bedbound or severity as a predictor of treatment response; its prognosis content is covered by the trials-recovery-rates link.

result: The delta-ACTH response to 100 ug ovine CRH was attenuated in CFS (21.0 vs 57.8 ng/L, p significant, df=21), and adding 10 ug desmopressin augmented and normalised the pituitary-adrenal response in CFS.
reason: Measures pituitary ACTH response to CRH (central drive), not cortisol response to ACTH or glucocorticoid suppression; no atlas finding covers CRH-stimulated ACTH. Candidate for a new central-HPA finding.

result: Desmopressin normalised an attenuated ACTH response to ovine CRH in CFS (delta-ACTH 21.0 vs 57.8 ng/L without DDAVP).
reason: Does not measure plasma vasopressin, osmolality or water handling; it tests DDAVP potentiation of CRH-induced ACTH release, which is a different question.

result: In a double-blind study of civilian and Gulf War veteran CFS patients vs matched controls, PCR of PBMC for HHV6, HHV7, EBV and CMV and serum anti-EBV and anti-HHV6 titres showed no significant differences, including after stratifying by psychiatric comorbidity and onset type.
reason: Independent cohort, same measure (EBV/HHV6 serology plus PCR), no difference; sample size not given in abstract.

result: 67 CFS patients (Oxford criteria) vs 126 matched controls showed impaired sustained-attention and response performance, with the group gap widening as acute fatigue developed over a long test session.
reason: Objective attention/reaction tasks show deficits in the same direction; within-session worsening is consistent with the finding's sustained-attention sensitivity note. Oxford criteria.

result: In 39 CFS vs 31 inactive controls on 45-min 70-degree tilt (impedance cardiography), CFS had higher heart rate and smaller pulsatile-systolic area at baseline and early tilt and smaller stroke volume among completers, but positive tilt rates (11 vs 12) and haemodynamic adjustments to tilt did not differ.
reason: Replicates smaller stroke volume vs inactive controls; note it did not find a greater fall on tilt, so it does not support that part of the claim.
